summary: Cells and batteries, safe charging, ampere-hours and run time, internal resistance, DC motors and generators, and motor current.

blocks.title: Cells and batteries
items: Cell: 2 different plates in an electrolyte. The chemical reaction makes a voltage.
Lead-acid: lead plates in sulfuric acid and water. Rechargeable, so it's a storage cell.
Series: + joined to −, so voltages add. 6 lead-acid cells make a 12-volt battery. 12 nickel-cadmium cells make 15 V.

blocks.title: Charging
items: Charging: a higher voltage drives current in backward, reversing the chemistry.
The hazard: near full charge, hydrogen gas escapes. It's explosive in air, so ventilate and keep sparks and flames away.

blocks.title: Motors and generators
items: Motor: electrical power into motion. Generator: the reverse.
Field winding: a fixed electromagnet. Armature: the coil that spins inside it, fed by brushes.
Generator voltage depends on speed and flux. A commutator, a rotating switch, gives DC.
Counter-EMF: a spinning armature also generates, pushing back on the supply. Weaker field, faster motor.

blocks.title: Generators in use
items: Shunt-wound DC generator: voltage is highest at no load, lowest at full load.
Voltage regulation means the voltage fluctuations from load to no-load, as a percentage of full-load volts. 110 V to 100 V is 10%.
Separately-excited AC generator: at constant speed, the amount of field current controls the output.

blocks.title: Exam traps
items: Charging's harm is hydrogen, not chlorine, oxygen or plate sulfation.
1.2 V isn't lead-acid. 1.5 V is alkaline, not nickel-cadmium.
Forget the 70% and you get the trap 249. Ignore the 50 watts.
28.97 is amperes, not hours. 1.0 A ignores internal resistance.
Voltage regulation isn't efficiency or a winding ratio.
Output follows field current, not the armature, brushes or exciter.
